title: Monthly Retail Trade benchmark revision — retail sales and inventories restated on the 2023 and 2024 Annual Integrated Economic Survey (DUPLICATE of census-benchmark-revision-nsa-2026-09-28; same Census release)
source: EST: two Census primaries re-fetched direct by THIS lane on 2026-09-06, independently of the proposal that named the id. census.gov/retail/index.html (HTTP 200, 743,183 bytes), announcements block, verbatim: "Intention to Revise: Monthly retail estimates are anticipated to be revised based on historical corrections and the results of the 2023 and 2024 Annual Integrated Economic Survey. Revised not adjusted estimates and corresponding adjusted estimates are tentatively scheduled for release on September 28, 2026 at 10:00 a.m. EDT." Corroborated on census.gov/mtis/index.html (HTTP 200, 684,348 bytes): "Revised not adjusted estimates and corresponding adjusted estimates are tentatively scheduled for release on September 28, 2026 and October 26, 2026, respectively." Stays estimate on Census's own word "tentatively", on the date's absence from census.gov/economic-indicators/calendar-listview.html, and on this lane's no-self-confirm limit for an in-sweep discovery. Checked 2026-09-06
notes: CANONICAL FILE WRITTEN 2026-09-06 by this event's own initial research, after reading the single proposal for this id (`from-mwts-benchmark-revision-2026-10-26`), which this file now shadows. THIS ID IS A DUPLICATE AND THE DUPLICATE IS THE FIRST FINDING. `census-benchmark-revision-nsa-2026-09-28` (canonical, merged 2026-09-06, PR #1772) is the SAME Census release — one 10:00 a.m. EDT restatement of Monthly Retail Trade on the 2023 and 2024 AIES. Two lanes discovered it independently on the same day from different pages and filed it under different slugs; neither lane may delete or overwrite the other's file (docs/process/EVENT-RESEARCH.md), so the calendar carries one release under two ids until someone with the authority retires one. RECOMMENDED DIRECTION, unchanged from the twin's: retire THIS id, keep `census-benchmark-revision-nsa-2026-09-28`, which already carries the older ledger, three forward tests and its own tracking issue — its `-nsa-` token is a misnomer (both ledgers agree 09-28 carries the not-adjusted AND the adjusted retail estimates) but a slug is not worth breaking those links for. IMPACT CORRECTED `medium` -> `low`, diverging from the proposal that named this id and aligning with the twin. The proposal argued medium because the retail series is the larger object than wholesale; this session MEASURED that it is (see below) and still files low, because size of restatement and tradeability are different questions: `symbols: []`, no macro-keyed house playbook, no consensus forecast for a restatement to surprise against, and the twin measured the 09-28 session class inert (SPY quarter-end-minus-2, n=66, median range 0.910% vs 0.904%, permutation p=0.942). The correction is also the cheapest thing this lane can do about the duplicate: `low` at D-22 reassesses every 30 days instead of every 7, so the duplicate lane costs roughly one more look rather than three. WHAT THIS SESSION MEASURED THAT NO LEDGER HAD. The twin recorded the retail magnitude as unmeasurable — ALFRED 404ed six times and FRED's CSV silently ignores `vintage_date`. Census publishes its own superseded vintages, and that route is open: www2.census.gov/retail/releases/historical/mrts/mrtssales92-present25.xlsx (HTTP 200, 428,539 bytes) is the MRTS sales workbook as published with data through 2025-02, against www.census.gov/retail/mrts/www/mrtssales92-present.xlsx (HTTP 200, 440,847 bytes) today. Every one of the 398 overlapping months of the headline not-adjusted series changed; of the 372 months before 2023, all 372 moved by at least 0.05%, median -2.098%, range -3.201% (1992) to -1.534%. 2023 restated -1.866% (-$154.7B), 2024 -1.894% (-$161.9B); the restated annual totals reproduce the twin's independent FRED reads of $8,139.5B and $8,386.0B exactly, which is what validates the parser. That window contains at least one annual revision plus a general-merchandise reclassification (three old kind-of-business rows replaced by two), so it is NOT attributable to one dated release — it establishes the SCALE of a retail restatement (whole history, every month, ~2%) against the wholesale sibling's 0.126% per month, and nothing about 09-28's own size. Research is not action: `estimate`-dated, no symbols, and a restatement of 2023-2024 history licenses no entry on any date.
